This artifact is materialized FIRST and the existing suite is run against it UNCHANGED, so that the set of controls the new lineage member actually breaks is OBSERVED rather than predicted from a read-only opening. Predicting it is unreliable in this suite: the lineage axis is carried by at least three different predicate shapes -- a bare existsSync, a dense-maximum pin with no path literal, and a JSON corpus scan -- and a textual sweep for the path literal alone is blind to the latter two.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.WHY_THEY_MUST_MOVE: There is no way to allocate this lineage position without falsifying them. Leaving them would leave the suite red; deleting them would remove the only mechanism that catches an over-allocation.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.POSTSTATE: Each existence assertion becomes a POSITIVE EXISTENCE PROOF: existsSync of the v1.0.37 path is TRUE. The predecessor existence proof for v1.0.36 is RETAINED alongside it in every case, so each pair reads as an advance rather than a replacement, and a deletion of either file is caught. The dense maximum advances from 36 to 37. The corpus scan is advanced to the NEXT unallocated pair -- version 1.0.38 and HPO-ODS-W2-35 -- which preserves its exact shape and its exact purpose while making it true again.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.THE_CORPUS_SCAN_IS_ADVANCED_NOT_DELETED: BINDING. The stray-copy predicate is the only control that would catch a second file carrying this version, or an addendum that quietly carries the next grant id. Deleting it to obtain a green would remove the control entirely. It is advanced, both disjuncts together, and remains a scan over every addendum in the directory.
FILESYSTEM_SENTINEL_DISPOSITION.THE_MECHANICALLY_NEXT_ABSENCE_SENTINEL_I: existsSync of docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_MAINTENANCE_ADDENDUM_v1.0.38.json is asserted FALSE. Without it the lineage axis would carry only positive assertions and a future over-allocation would pass unnoticed.
